newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee easier, supply ample.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee easier, supply ample.

text.p: Indonesian Robusta coffee prices were easier on Tuesday following slight declines in London overnight, traders said.
They said the local price was quoted at 3,200-3,250 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, down from 3,250-3,300 rupiah a week ago.
The export price was quoted at $1,390-$1,400/tonne FOB Lampung, compared with $1,400-$1,420 last week.
"When prices in London decline, farmers begin to hold back supplies," one trader said. "They are well aware of price movements in London and hold out for better prices."
"There is some caution in the market on expectations of lower production this year, and players are trying to make sure that they will not be caught short," the trader said.

Oesman Soedargo, chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters, said last Monday the country's production was expected to fall by some 30 percent this year from an original forecast of 480,000 tonnes due to bad weather. He said the total exportable volume would amount to 220,000 tonnes.
Traders generally agreed that there would be a drop in output this year, but some said they expected to the shortfall to range between 10 and 20 percent.
"It will be difficult to tell unless you carry out a survey of the growing regions, especially in the South Sumatra coffee triangle," one trader said.
"At this point in time, almost everyone agrees there will be a fall in production," he said. "But by how much...will depend on each player's estimate based on the information he has."
The trader said heavy rains and strong winds had affected the flowering process in the highland in South Sumatra, but added that at the moment supply seemed steady.
"Only when the market feels the squeeze will you see players moving to cover positions," he added.
